question: Early in round 2 you tried to save a round-1 reference render by copying the round-1 binary into the out/ folder and running it from there. Did that run produce the reference image? If not, what error did it print?
answer:
No — that run produced no reference image, and it failed before any rendering started.

What happened (my own earlier action, archive messages #55-#57): I ran
  cp pathtracer/pathtracer out/pathtracer_r1 && ./out/pathtracer_r1 --scene-config scene-default.json --seed 1 --threads 8 --spp 64 --benchmark 1 --out out/r1_default.ppm --out-pfm out/r1_default.pfm
The copy itself succeeded (the directory listing shows out/pathtracer_r1, 101112 bytes), but the program printed exactly:
  metal init error: cannot read shared shader header
and exited with code 1. The follow-up `shasum out/r1_default.pfm` then reported `shasum: out/r1_default.pfm: No such file or directory`, and the listing confirms neither r1_default.ppm nor r1_default.pfm was ever created — so there is no round-1 reference render from that attempt.

Why: the host resolves both the shader directory and the shared struct header relative to argv[0] (executable_directory(argv[0]) + "/shaders" and "/include/pt_gpu_types.hpp"). Running the binary from out/ made it look for out/include/pt_gpu_types.hpp, which does not exist — the .metal sources are compiled from disk at startup, so the binary is not self-contained. I recorded the lesson in my log/notes (archive index line for #56-#57): never run a copied binary from out/; run it in place, or in a snapshot directory that has include/ and shaders/ next to it. For round-1 comparison I therefore used the already-rendered round-1 outputs (out/round1_default.pfm, sha1 87c956f4...) plus bit-identity checks against a fixed seed-7 PFM generated in the live source directory.
